verdict.rationale: Capacities documents its own REST API, published at api.capacities.io with an OpenAPI 3.0 spec. The API uses bearer-token authentication and has a TypeScript SDK (npm install @capacities/api), so content can be read and written programmatically without the app UI, which is the basis for headless automation from scripts or CI. However, nothing documents a headless or CLI mode, or CI usage specifically, and the Beta API is being discontinued on September 1, 2026. Missing for 10: an official CLI or headless runtime, CI-specific guidance or examples (service tokens, pipeline usage), and hands-on corroboration of automated use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The Capacities API is a REST API that allows you access, create and manipulate your content.
The Capacities REST API gives you programmatic access to a workspace space — read and write objects, properties, block content, daily notes, and more.
The Capacities API uses Bearer authentication (token-based authentication, OAuth 2.0 RFC 6750).
Install the Capacities TypeScript SDK: npm install @capacities/api
